subtitle: std::basic_string_view<CharT,Traits> — C++17's non-owning read-only character view. restd back-ports the full C++17 surface to C++11 across seven granular headers, with the minimal char_traits needed to support it reaching C++98 on the char/wchar_t paths. SHIPPED: char_traits (generic primary + char/wchar_t/char16_t/char32_t/char8_t specialisations), basic_string_view with the complete member surface (construction, iterators + reverse, capacity, access, modifiers, copy, substr, six-way compare, the six find-family operations), the four C++11 view aliases + u8string_view (C++20), the deleted nullptr_t constructor (back-ported from C++23), starts_with/ends_with (back-ported from C++20) and contains (back-ported from C++23), the comparison operators (six legacy on C++11-C++17, operator== + operator<=> on C++20+), the operator""sv literals, and restd::hash specialisations for all five aliases. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: 6-year back-port to C++11; constexpr from C++14 (std reached it in C++17). DEFERRED: operator<< (needs <ostream>), the C++20 contiguous-iterator/sentinel constructor, and the C++23 range constructor. DIVERGENCES: char_traits ships the string-view-supporting subset (no off_type/pos_type/state_type, no comparison_category); operator<=> yields strong_ordering directly rather than consulting Traits::comparison_category; hash values are self-contained and not required to match any std::hash.
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++17 <string_view> header. Shipped on C++11+ (back-port of the C++17 surface); char_traits' char/wchar_t paths reach C++98. starts_with/ends_with (C++20) and contains (C++23) back-ported to C++11. Constexpr from C++14 (ahead of std's C++17). operator<<, the C++20 iterator/sentinel constructor, and the C++23 range constructor deferred.

symbols.name: char_traits
symbols.notes: Generic primary (internal::char_traits_base<_CharT,_IntT> shared implementation) plus the standard specialisations: char and wchar_t compile on C++98, char16_t/char32_t are gated on C++11, char8_t on C++20. String-view-supporting subset only — carries char_type, int_type, and the comparison/search/copy static operations (assign, eq, lt, compare, length, find, move, copy, to_char_type, to_int_type, eq_int_type, eof, not_eof). Deliberately omits off_type/pos_type/state_type (iostream-only) and the C++20 comparison_category member, to avoid <iosfwd>/<cwchar>/<compare> deps. char specialisation compares as unsigned char per the standard; wchar_t int_type is wint_t/WEOF (<cwchar>), char16_t/char32_t use uint_least16_t/uint_least32_t (<cstdint>), char8_t uses unsigned int. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: the search/length/compare ops are constexpr from C++14 (std waited for C++17 / P0426); the trivial element ops (eq, lt, assign(1)) are constexpr from C++11.

symbols.name: basic_string_view<CharT,Traits>
symbols.notes: Read-only (pointer, length) view owning nothing. Full C++17 member surface: default/copy/(ptr,count)/(ptr) constructors, iterators (begin/end/cbegin/cend + reverse rbegin/rend/crbegin/crend via restd::reverse_iterator), capacity (size/length/empty/max_size), access (operator[]/at/front/back/data — at() throws std::out_of_range when <stdexcept> is available, aborts otherwise), modifiers (remove_prefix/remove_suffix/swap), copy, substr, the six compare() overloads, and all six find-family operations (find, rfind, find_first_of, find_last_of, find_first_not_of, find_last_not_of) with four overloads each. npos uses a guarded pre-C++17 out-of-class definition. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: 6-year back-port of the C++17 interface to C++11; trivial observers are constexpr from C++11, the loop/mutating ops from C++14 (std reached full constexpr in C++17). Back-ported members starts_with/ends_with (std C++20) and contains (std C++23) are catalogued on their own rows.
symbols.failure_reason: Floored at C++11 by design: the deleted nullptr_t constructor, the char16_t/char32_t alias support, the operator""sv literals, and the constexpr surface are all C++11 language features. A bare runtime (pointer, length) core could mechanically compile on C++98, but shipping it without constexpr, UDLs, or the Unicode aliases would be a crippled view divergent from the C++17 surface this module back-ports, so a C++98 path was not pursued.

symbols.name: string_view / wstring_view / u16string_view / u32string_view
symbols.notes: The standard convenience aliases of basic_string_view for char, wchar_t, char16_t, char32_t. Available from C++11 in restd (std introduced them in C++17).
symbols.failure_reason: Aliases of basic_string_view, which is floored at C++11 (see its row). char16_t/char32_t are themselves C++11 types, so u16string_view/u32string_view cannot precede C++11 regardless.

symbols.name: u8string_view
symbols.notes: Alias of basic_string_view<char8_t>. Tracks char8_t, hence C++20.
symbols.failure_reason: char8_t is a C++20 language feature; u8string_view cannot exist before C++20. Matches std (also C++20) — no back-port possible.

symbols.name: basic_string_view(nullptr_t) = delete
symbols.notes: Deleted constructor that forbids building a view from a null pointer literal (string_view sv = nullptr; is ill-formed). Back-ported from std's C++23 to C++11.
symbols.failure_reason: Deleted functions are a C++11 language feature; the back-port cannot reach C++98. Back-ported from std's C++23 to C++11 — a 12-year reach.

symbols.name: starts_with / ends_with
symbols.notes: Member prefix/suffix queries, three overloads each (basic_string_view, CharT, const CharT*). Back-ported from std's C++20 to C++11; constexpr from C++14 (std from C++20).
symbols.failure_reason: Members of basic_string_view, which is floored at C++11 (see its row). Back-ported from std's C++20 to C++11.

symbols.name: contains
symbols.notes: Member substring/character containment query, three overloads (basic_string_view, CharT, const CharT*), expressed via find(). Back-ported from std's C++23 to C++11; constexpr from C++14.
symbols.failure_reason: Member of basic_string_view, which is floored at C++11 (see its row). Back-ported from std's C++23 to C++11.

symbols.name: operator==
symbols.notes: Non-member equality. One operand is a non-deduced context via the local internal::sv_identity (a type_identity stand-in) so a convertible operand (e.g. const CharT*) is accepted on either side. Survives the C++20 rewrite. Constexpr from C++14 (std C++17).
symbols.failure_reason: Depends on basic_string_view, which is floored at C++11. Back-ported from std's C++17 to C++11.

symbols.name: operator!= / < / <= / > / >=
symbols.notes: The five legacy relational operators, each with the sv_identity non-deduced operand. Gated out on C++20+ (#if !D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP20_OR_HIGHER), where the compiler synthesises them from operator<=>. Constexpr from C++14 (std C++17).
symbols.failure_reason: Depends on basic_string_view (C++11 floor). Back-ported from std's C++17 to C++11. Removed/synthesised on C++20+ — the explicit overloads are the only way to call them on C++11-C++17.

symbols.name: operator<=>
symbols.notes: Three-way comparison yielding std::strong_ordering (from <compare>). The C++20 Traits::comparison_category hook is not consulted — strong_ordering is produced directly (documented minor divergence). sv_identity non-deduced operand as for operator==.
symbols.failure_reason: operator<=> is a C++20 language feature; cannot be back-ported. The six legacy relational operators cover C++11-C++17.

symbols.name: operator""sv
symbols.notes: User-defined literals in restd::literals::string_view_literals (a doubly-inline namespace, mirroring std). One overload per built-in character type; the char8_t overload is gated on C++20. Each yields the matching view over the literal's data/length. The reserved-suffix diagnostic is suppressed per-compiler so -Wall -Wextra stays clean. constexpr from C++11 (single-return; std from C++17).
symbols.failure_reason: User-defined literals are a C++11 language feature; cannot reach C++98. Back-ported from std's C++17 to C++11.

symbols.name: hash<string_view> / wstring_view / u16string_view / u32string_view
symbols.notes: restd::hash specialisations for the four C++11 view aliases. Self-contained polynomial roll over the character units (internal::sv_hash_bytes) — stable within restd but NOT required to agree with any std::hash value (restd::string does not exist yet). Back-ported from std's C++17 to C++11.
symbols.failure_reason: Specialises restd::hash (shipped in <functional>); floored at C++11 with the rest of the module.

symbols.name: hash<u8string_view>
symbols.notes: restd::hash specialisation for u8string_view. Same self-contained roll as the other view hashes; gated on C++20 with char8_t.
symbols.failure_reason: Specialises restd::hash<u8string_view>; u8string_view (hence this specialisation) is C++20+ because char8_t is C++20.

symbols.name: operator<< (ostream insertion)
symbols.notes: Deferred. The standard's ostream inserter for basic_string_view needs the iostream subsystem. Tracked here so the Coverage Failures sheet surfaces it.
symbols.failure_reason: Deferred — needs the iostream subsystem (restd <ostream>, priority 79), not yet shipped.

symbols.name: basic_string_view(It first, End last)
symbols.notes: Deferred. The C++20 contiguous-iterator / sentinel constructor. The (pointer, length) and null-terminated (pointer) constructors cover the common cases in the interim.
symbols.failure_reason: Deferred — needs the C++20 contiguous_iterator concept (not yet shipped) plus iterator/sentinel difference plumbing.

symbols.name: basic_string_view(R&& r)
symbols.notes: Deferred. The C++23 range constructor (explicit). Its building blocks ranges::data and ranges::size are shipped, but the contiguous-range / borrowed-range constraint is left for a focused follow-up.
symbols.failure_reason: Deferred — the C++23 range constructor needs a contiguous-range / borrowed-range constraint wired over ranges::data + ranges::size (both shipped); deferred to keep the initial back-port scoped to the C++17 surface.
